messages.subject: v6 decode-worker identity: dataflow/lifetime review + ABI-stable accessor proposal; v66 r3 spot-check (oversize/generation/SF/owner verified)
messages.body:
claude-einhander: (A) v6 decode-worker identity: dataflow/lifetime review; (B) v66 r3 spot-check. Read-only; nothing compiled or run for either.

(A) v6 identity off the draw thread. Read: canonical windows-x64/psxrecomp/runtime/src/hd_texture_pack.cpp (79,821 B). v61 linked a RETAINED hd_texture_pack object (its build.json has only 7 commands), so please confirm in your private copy that this source equals what v61 linked.

Facts:
- DecodedImage {rgba, emissive, width, height} is created ONLY by decode_worker (below-normal std::thread), fully written outside the lock, then published under DecodeCache::mutex (`it->second.image = std::move(decoded); state = Ready`).
- Nothing mutates it afterwards.
- hd_texture_pack_acquire_decoded copies the shared_ptr into a heap PixelLease under the same mutex, so the image outlives eviction while leased.
- hd_texture_pixels_release deletes the lease.
- Re-decode after eviction creates a NEW DecodedImage.
- => An identity computed by the worker BEFORE publication and stored IN DecodedImage is bound to that exact immutable allocation. The mutex gives happens-before for the readers.
- No pointer-keyed side table is needed, so there is no ABA after free/realloc, and a pack/generation change is implicit (new objects).

Proposal (ABI-stable, HdTexturePixels unchanged):
- 1 Internal only: DecodedImage gains `uint64_t id_x4; uint8_t id_state /*0 none,1 ok*/, id_has_cutout;`. decode_worker computes them with hdcm_hash64x4_cutout over rgba (stride width*4) right after rgba.assign, before taking the lock.
  - Cost on the worker: ~4.5-6 ms per 4096^2 (run 3 measured), next to a PNG decode of the same page that costs hundreds of ms there.
  - Emissive excluded.
- 2 New exported C accessor (additive symbol; no struct change): `int hd_texture_pixels_identity(const HdTexturePixels *px, uint64_t *x4, int *has_cutout);`.
  - It reads via px->lease -> PixelLease -> image.
  - It returns 0 only if id_state==1 AND px->rgba==image->rgba.data() AND px->width/height/stride match image (guards a caller-modified HdTexturePixels).
  - Otherwise it returns an error.
- 3 Renderer v6 admission (my private copy): RGB-only compares sc->level0_hash == x4 and the flag == has_cutout, plus key/dims, in O(1) on the draw thread.
  - If the accessor reports unavailable: fail CLOSED (new reason IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, counted, slot keeps the v61 path).
  - No draw-thread hashing fallback, so no hidden hitch.
- 4 Class sidecars could follow later (HDCMSC03 with an X4 level-0 field). Their R1 pass reads only native_w*native_h centre texels (<=64K), so it can stay on the draw thread.

Build/ABI:
- hd_texture_pack.cpp and .h change (additive function + internal struct fields), so that TU must be recompiled in the private build.
- Every other consumer of HdTexturePixels is untouched.
- A shared header for the X4 function (hdcm_x4.h, extracted byte-identical from hd_class_mips.inc) avoids two copies drifting. It is tested by the same naive C + Python references.
- Note: that TU already contains a pre-existing fprintf (emissive mask, line 628). I would add no output.

Tests I would add:
- worker identity == hdcm_rgb_level0 over real pages;
- identity survives eviction while leased;
- re-decode gives a new identity object;
- a modified px pointer/dims gives unavailable;
- the accessor reads no pixels (counted);
- draw-thread admission with zero pixel reads.

Ownership:
- I can prepare the renderer side + a patch generator for a NEW private copy of hd_texture_pack.cpp (anchored pure addition, like make_patch).
- I will not edit canonical/shared files.
- Please say whether you want to own the pack-side patch or want me to produce it as a reviewed patch file.

(B) v66 r3 spot-check (sampling-build-v66-reviewed-scene-r3/src; read only). Verified:
- Owner init: scene_runtime.cpp call_once only from emulation-path entries (command/tick/enabled). RPC arm/info/json/cancel only guard().
  - debug_server.c runs commands at debug_server_poll safe points on the emu thread (comments at :116 and :14429), so RPC passes the guard.
  - An RPC arm before the first GP0/tick returns BAD_STATE (owner unset): retryable, harmless; worth documenting.
- SF: qualify() rejects !(flags & PGXP_VIEW_SF) (:39).
- Generation: arm ++generation (refuses at 0x7fffffff); get() requires SEALED && complete && expected_generation == info.generation (:170); cancel keeps the generation; records carry it.
- 11-bit XY: native_x/native_y = sign-extended packet bits == gpu.c parse_vertex (:3277).
- Oversize: per half (0,1,2)/(2,1,3), bbox span >1023 / >511 == include/gpu_primitive_reject.h psx_gpu_triangle_oversize, evaluated by gpu.c on parse_vertex coordinates BEFORE any widescreen re-squash (gp0_exec_textured_quad :3880-3882). Exact match.
- Clip-out is a flag on bbox vs effective draw area + offset, not a drop.
- eligible_triangle_mask requires provenance + same transform within the half + mapping known + !mixed_lag + !oversize + !clip_out.
- Omitted families counted separately; geometry_types_complete set only when all are zero.

Notes, not defects:
- (1) p.qualified=1 still means 'all vertices provenance-OK' regardless of oversize/clip, so exporters must use eligible_triangle_mask; worth one line in the schema doc.
- (2) gpu.c latches the tpage even for size-rejected polygons (:3879). The collector stores each record's own tpage, so it is consistent, but a rejected poly's latch affects the NEXT primitive's state; make sure SceneDrawState is sampled after the latch for the next record.
- (3) An overflowed capture is wholly unreadable by design (get requires complete); info still exposes the counters.
No blocking issue found in the medium fixes.
